problem.summary: YOLOv3 is presented as an incremental set of fixes to YOLO: accuracy on COCO still lagged RetinaNet on the average-AP metric, localization degrades at higher IOU thresholds, small/medium/large object trade-offs remained uneven, and the authors question whether the COCO metric itself measures what matters.
statements: Box alignment quality drops as the IOU threshold rises, so localization is imperfect.
Small objects were historically a weakness of YOLO and medium/large object performance is comparatively worse.
On COCO average AP (.5-.95 IOU) YOLOv3 trails RetinaNet-style detectors.
The COCO mAP metric may emphasize box precision over classification in ways practitioners do not care about.

evidence.quote: However, performance drops significantly as the IOU threshold increases indicating YOLOv3 struggles to get the boxes perfectly aligned with the object.
In the past YOLO struggled with small objects.
However, it has comparatively worse performance on medium and larger size objects. More investigation is needed to get to the bottom of this.
mAP is already screwed up because all that matters is per-class rank ordering.

background.summary: The report builds directly on YOLO9000/YOLOv2 (dimension-cluster anchors), borrows the multi-scale idea from FPN, the speed/accuracy comparison framing from the Focal Loss paper, and residual-network design from ResNets; the authors are explicit that most components are adopted ideas rather than new ones.

relatedWork.name: YOLO9000 / YOLOv2
relatedWork.relation: immediate predecessor whose anchor-cluster formulation is kept
relatedWork.quote: Following YOLO9000 our system predicts bounding boxes using dimension clusters as anchor boxes [15].

relatedWork.name: Feature Pyramid Networks
relatedWork.relation: prior multi-scale feature design mirrored by YOLOv3's three-scale predictions
relatedWork.quote: Our system extracts features from those scales using a similar concept to feature pyramid networks [8].

relatedWork.name: Faster R-CNN
relatedWork.relation: two-stage baseline whose dual IOU threshold training scheme was tried and rejected
relatedWork.quote: Faster RCNN uses two IOU thresholds during training.

relatedWork.name: Darknet-19 / ResNets
relatedWork.relation: backbone predecessors combined into the new Darknet-53 extractor
relatedWork.quote: Our new network is a hybrid approach between the network used in YOLOv2, Darknet-19, and that newfangled residual network stuff.

evidence.quote: So here’s the deal with YOLOv3: We mostly took good ideas from other people.
We also trained a new classifier network that’s better than the other ones.

solution.summary: YOLOv3 combines a new 53-layer residual backbone (Darknet-53) with three-scale FPN-like predictions, k-means anchor priors, logistic-regression objectness, and multilabel classification with independent logistic classifiers trained by binary cross-entropy.
solution.approach: Detect at three scales on a residual Darknet-53 backbone using k-means anchor boxes, sigmoid-constrained center offsets and exponentiated size offsets, with independent per-class logistic classifiers.
components: Darknet-53 feature extractor with 53 convolutional layers and shortcut connections
9 k-means clustered anchor priors split across 3 scales
three-scale prediction with 2x upsampling and concatenation
logistic regression objectness with one assigned prior per ground truth
multilabel classification with independent logistic classifiers (no softmax)
multi-scale training, data augmentation and batch normalization

evidence.quote: YOLOv3 predicts boxes at 3 different scales.
We still use k-means clustering to determine our bounding box priors.
YOLOv3 predicts an objectness score for each bounding box using logistic regression.
Each box predicts the classes the bounding box may contain using multilabel classification.

experiments.summary: The report tabulates COCO test-dev AP/AP50/AP75 and size-specific AP against two-stage and one-stage detectors, ImageNet backbone accuracy/speed for Darknet-53, and speed-accuracy curves on an M40/Titan X, plus an informal list of ideas that were tried and failed.

evidence.quote: At 320 × 320 YOLOv3 runs in 22 ms at 28.2 mAP, as accurate as SSD but three times faster.
It achieves 57.9 AP50 in 51 ms on a Titan X, compared to 57.5 AP50 in 198 ms by RetinaNet, similar performance but 3.8× faster.
Darknet-53 is better than ResNet-101 and 1.5× faster.

limitations.summary: The authors freely admit YOLOv3 is not as strong on COCO average AP, is weaker on medium/large objects, and that several attempted improvements (focal loss, linear x/y offsets, dual IOU thresholds) hurt or failed to help.
items: Localization quality falls off as the IOU threshold increases (AP75 34.4 versus AP50 57.9).
Comparatively worse performance on medium and large objects despite improved small-object APS.
On COCO average AP (.5-.95) YOLOv3 (33.0) remains behind RetinaNet (39.1).
Focal loss, linear x/y offset prediction and dual IOU thresholds were all tried and reduced mAP or destabilized training.

evidence.quote: It’s not as great on the COCO average AP between .5 and .95 IOU metric.
We tried using focal loss. It dropped our mAP about 2 points.
We tried lots of stuff while we were working on YOLOv3. A lot of it didn’t work.

futureDirections.direction: Investigate why medium/large object performance lagged despite strong APS.
futureDirections.quote: More investigation is needed to get to the bottom of this.

futureDirections.direction: Revisit the rejected training techniques with tuning to stabilize training.
futureDirections.quote: It is possible that some of these techniques could eventually produce good results, perhaps they just need some tuning to stabilize the training.

futureDirections.direction: Develop evaluation metrics that reflect what practitioners actually care about.
futureDirections.quote: if we’re going to come up with new metrics we should focus on these discrepancies

equations.name: Box prediction decode
equations.expr: bx = sigmoid(tx) + cx, by = sigmoid(ty) + cy, bw = pw * e^tw, bh = ph * e^th

applications.detail: The authors cite benign uses of detectors such as counting zebras in a national park and tracking a pet camera, while stressing that computer vision is also being put to questionable use.
applications.quote: counting the number of zebras in a national park [13]

applications.detail: The discussion section explicitly raises personal-data harvesting and military funding as harms researchers should consider and mitigate.
applications.quote: computer vision is already being put to questionable use and as researchers we have a responsibility to at least consider the harm our work might be doing and think of ways to mitigate it.

deploymentClaims: YOLOv3 runs at 22 ms (320x320 input), 29 ms (416) and 51 ms (608) on an M40 or Titan X.
Darknet-53 reaches 78 FPS at 256x256 on a Titan X with 18.7B ops.
All the code is online at https://pjreddie.com/yolo/

evidence.quote: Times from either an M40 or Titan X, they are basically the same GPU.
Run times are measured on a Titan X at 256 × 256.
